f133.summary: Paris three weeks after the Barricades: the informant explains why Nevers should not go to the King unsummoned, reports that everyone wants Nevers at court and that Paris is sending deputies to the King; the curés of St André and St Benoît stir up the people, and the new League municipality under the prévôt La Chapelle is steered by Guise's council, while the échevin Cotteblanche refused to let the Arsenal's artillery go to Corbeil without the King's leave.
f133.en:
> I am very sorry that you took in bad part what was written to 24 [...] But because before his departure he offered
> 11 to stay if there were need, it was thought that he was even better than then, and consequently, without danger to
> his person, he could approach the King. Now we had well considered that if Nevers went to see 11 without
> being summoned out of affection, he might receive some worse treatment there [...] Secondly, 24 may remember that,
> when he was at La Cassine, 11 wrote to him only under compulsion, and nevertheless after he had come he
> welcomed him and did him honours [...] Thirdly, everyone wants Nevers at court much more than they did then. And
> not only the Leaguers but also the others [...] a rumour that 102 is sending deputies back to 11 charged [...]

f139.summary: The prévôt des marchands has returned to the Bastille; notaries seek money at interest guaranteed by Neuilly, Marcel, the prévôt and échevins; the Grand Écuyer courts Guise; it is held certain that the King will grant Guise the lieutenance générale and so there will be peace. Every run carries a contemporary gloss, and all agree with the key.
f139.en:
> It is a true thing that the prévôt des marchands has gone back to put himself in the Bastille. I have not been able
> to discover truly that any levy of money is being made. But I have certainly been assured, notably by 38
> [Garrault], that notaries are seeking money at interest, for which Nilly, Marcel, the prévôt des marchands
> and the échevins stand surety. But many have made difficulty about lending any, and for my part I am astonished
> that Marcel is mixed up in it. They say that 107 [the Grand Écuyer] is insinuating himself into the good
> graces of 9 [Guise] and presses him. His brother has also left 10 [Épernon].

snip.cap: BnF fr. 3976 f. 133v: the runs for par ruses et faulx bruictz, le prevost Chapelle, conseil de 9 et 106, and nommé Cotteblanche
snip.credit: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3976 f. 133v, via Gallica view 224

system: Clear letter with inserted runs in a homophonic, partly polyphonic letter-and-figure substitution (signs of one character or 1+character), plus bare code numbers for persons and places, some embedded in runs.
